track.note: The CS study path (DECISIONS C11; spec in docs/cst-track.md). Same phase, block, item, gate and question shape as step.json, so the same screens serve both. Edit freely: scripts/cambridge/scrape.mjs never adds or removes a track item; it refreshes only links, siteTitle and verified flags (Part IA course links come from tripos.parts.IA). Question lists are yours: supervision work is seeded where the course materials give exercise sheets, and empty lists are for you to fill.

supervisorPrompt.note: Code questions may be answered in OCaml, Java, C++ or Python. For foundation items, {course} is the item title.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.do: Four sub-parts, side by side: proof, maths, functional programming, and the pre-arrival checklist. Cambridge expects no programming on arrival; the maths is the real gap. FoCS "aims to correct" imperative habits, so the functional part matters even for a strong programmer.
phases.note: Each sub-part has its own gate (+200 XP each). Part IA unlocks when all four pass.

phases.name: Part IA
phases.do: Courses in Paper order, following the stated prerequisites. Each course: lecture notes, supervision exercises (from the materials), and past-paper questions by topic, run through the loop (cold attempt, write-up, supervision, redo). NST Part IA Mathematics runs alongside, with the example sheets in courses.json / DAMTP.

pace.text: 2 courses at a time, 1 supervision each per week

gate.text: Per paper: a timed past paper with 3 of 5 questions at least 14/20.

evidence.label: Paper 1: questions at 14/20 or more (need 3 of 5)
Paper 2: questions at 14/20 or more (need 3 of 5)
Paper 3: questions at 14/20 or more (need 3 of 5)

suggestedOrder.label: suggested
suggestedOrder.note: Two courses at a time. The pairs respect the stated prerequisites: Algorithms 2 after Algorithms 1, Introduction to Probability after Discrete Mathematics, Operating Systems after Digital Electronics. Cambridge teaches them by term, not in this order.

phases.note: Exam structure (2026, https://www.cl.cam.ac.uk/teaching/exams/exam-structure.pdf): answer 5 questions on each paper, each marked out of 20. Paper 1: FoCS, OOP, Introduction to Probability, Algorithms 1, Algorithms 2, one each. Paper 2: Digital Electronics, Operating Systems, Software and Security Engineering, one each, and 2 on Discrete Mathematics. Paper 3: Databases, Introduction to Graphics, Interaction Design, one each, and 2 on Machine Learning and Real-world Data. Part IA has no weight in the degree class but must be passed (https://www.cst.cam.ac.uk/teaching/exams/marking-and-classing). Materials are 2025-26 where the 2026-27 pages are empty.

phases.name: Part IB
